reference.title: Cable Straight Arm Pulldown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you sweep the bar down to the thighs, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can sweep down with straight arms and a still trunk.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; 1 s pause at the thighs

cues.text: Stand facing the high pulley, feet hip width, knees soft, hips back so the trunk leans about 25 degrees forward with a flat back; hold the bar overhand about shoulder width, arms long and raised in front, elbows softly bent.
Breathe out and sweep the bar down in an arc to the front of the thighs, arms staying straight, shoulders down.
Bar at the thighs, lats tight, chest proud; do not bend the elbows.
Breathe in and let the bar rise in the same arc until the arms are about level with the head.
Brief pause with the lats stretched, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows and pushing the bar down like a pushdown
mistakes.fix: Keep the soft bend fixed; the movement is only at the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the trunk up and down
mistakes.fix: Hold the hinge still; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back or shrugging at the top
mistakes.fix: Keep the back flat and the shoulders away from the ears.
Control the return through the whole arc.

kinematics.norm: From arms about level with the head to the bar at the thighs (clinical opinion); pullover-type shoulder extension exercises load the lats (Teixeira 2022)
Soft and unchanged, about 10-20 degrees (clinical opinion)
Hinged about 20-30 degrees forward with a flat back, still (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Straight Arm Pulldown, video (movement reference)

Teixeira, Gomes, da Silva, Magalhães and Marchetti 2022, differences between pullover and pulldown exercises on maximal isometric force and myoelectric activity in recreationally-trained men (Int J Exerc Sci 15(4):797-807; PMC9362894)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the shoulder, elbow or back, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with straight arms and a still trunk.
Stand far enough back that the bar can rise to head height without pulling you forward.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort at the top: start the arc lower, around shoulder height (clinical opinion).
Back discomfort: stand more upright with less hinge and a lighter load.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the straight arm down and back to the side.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover: pulls the straight arm down and back to the side.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Long head helps extend the shoulder and holds the elbow straight.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Long head helps extend the shoulder and holds the elbow straight.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps extend the shoulder late in the arc.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps extend the shoulder late in the arc.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Set the shoulder blades down and back.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Set the shoulder blades down and back.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk still against the cable.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back flat in the hinge.
